questions.q: What does the FORCESEEK hint do?
options: Rebuilds every index on the table before the query runs
Forces the optimizer to always use a table scan regardless of indexes
Forces the query to run with MAXDOP 1
Forces the optimizer to produce an index seek (optionally against a named index) instead of a scan, for that one query
questions.explain: FORCESEEK constrains the optimizer's access-path choice for that specific query to a seek, optionally against a named index.

questions.q: What does OPTION (MAXDOP n) change, and what does it leave untouched?
options: It disables all query hints for the rest of the session
It forces the query to always run in parallel across every available core
It overrides the degree of parallelism for that one query only, leaving the instance-level max degree of parallelism setting untouched
It permanently changes the server's max degree of parallelism setting for every future query
questions.explain: OPTION (MAXDOP n) is a query-level override; the server-wide configuration everyone else's queries use is unaffected.

questions.q: Why is the USE PLAN hint described as brittle?
options: USE PLAN is deprecated and throws a syntax error in every current SQL Server version
USE PLAN requires rebuilding the entire database before it can take effect
The pinned plan XML is tied to the exact schema and statistics that existed when it was captured, and can silently stop being achievable if either drifts
USE PLAN can only be used with SELECT statements that return zero rows
questions.explain: Because the XML captures an exact plan shape tied to a specific schema/statistics snapshot, later changes can make that shape unachievable, and SQL Server falls back to compiling normally.

questions.q: What is the key advantage of sp_query_store_force_plan over hard-coding a FORCESEEK or USE PLAN hint directly in application code?
options: It permanently deletes all other cached plans for that query so only one can ever be used again
It forces an already-captured plan by plan_id with no code change required, and is reversible in one statement (sp_query_store_unforce_plan), visible in Query Store's own views
It requires a full server restart to take effect, unlike a hint
It automatically rewrites the query text to remove all hints
questions.explain: Forcing a plan via Query Store requires no application deployment to apply or remove, and the forced state is auditable directly in Query Store's views.

questions.q: A query has a known-good plan captured in its Query Store history but occasionally reverts to a worse plan after a statistics update. Per this lesson, what's the most surgical way to guarantee the good plan going forward?
options: Add WITH (FORCESEEK) to every query against that table
Disable Query Store entirely so no plan history is kept
EXEC sys.sp_query_store_force_plan, specifying that query's query_id and the known-good plan's plan_id
Rewrite the query to remove all WHERE clause filters
questions.explain: sp_query_store_force_plan pins that specific captured plan for that query_id going forward, without touching the application's query text at all.
